correctness.rationale: Strong density implies contraction consistency; finite pairwise winners make a transitive tournament because any directed triangle contradicts selected winner of a triple; the resulting unique total order represents all choices. Comparing a selected suffix winner with the choice on each later two-element set proves four-point necessity. Conversely pairwise suffix coherence implies all subsets have identical minima across the relevant two orders. Exhaustive independent semantic checks through four worlds and two distinct implementations reproduce counts. The infinite-size assertion depends on mathematical proof, not exhaustive code.

value.rationale: The exact structure of total functional strong density matters to conditional selection semantics: ranking representations compress exponential subset-selection tables into permutations and replace an exponentially many-subset test with O(n^4) four-world comparisons. Its smallest restrictive size, labelled counts, and isomorphism classes supply intrinsic finite-frame invariants for Boolean conditional algebra examples; these are not textbook relabellings or merely known chain counts.
